title: Hyaluronic acid and other adherence compounds in embryo transfer media for assisted reproductive technologies.
abstract: Successful implantation of the embryo into the endometrial lining is a key step in in vitro fertilisation (IVF). Adherence compounds such as hyaluronic acid (HA) and fibrin sealant are sometimes added to the embryo transfer medium to increase the likelihood of embryo implantation and pregnancy. This is the third update of a Cochrane review first published in the Cochrane Library in 2010. To determine whether adding adherence compounds to embryo transfer media improves pregnancy outcomes, includi…

title: The role of high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation in adults with mature T-cell lymphomas.
abstract: Mature T-cell lymphomas (MTCL) are a rare, heterogeneous group of malignant tumours arising from mature T lymphocytes, generally associated with a poor prognosis. Polychemotherapy has long been the standard treatment for most MTCL subtypes. High-dose therapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (autoSCT) and allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT) have been investigated to improve overall survival (OS). Given the rarity and poor prognosis of MTCL, an up-to-date…

title: Mifepristone versus other interventions for the prevention of pregnancy in reproductive-age women using emergency contraception.
abstract: Emergency contraception uses drugs or intrauterine devices to prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse. Understanding the effectiveness, safety, and acceptability of the various methods available is critical for reproductive healthcare providers and their patients. To evaluate the effectiveness, safety, and acceptability of mifepristone compared to other interventions in reproductive-age women using emergency contraception for the prevention of pregnancy. title: Pathogen-reduced platelets for the prevention of bleeding.
abstract: Platelet transfusions are used to prevent and treat bleeding in people who are thrombocytopenic (they have a low blood platelet count). Despite improvements in donor screening and laboratory testing, a small risk of viral, bacterial, or protozoal contamination of platelets remains. There is also an ongoing risk from newly emerging blood transfusion-transmitted infections (TTIs), for which laboratory tests may not be available at the initial outbreak. The risk of blood TTIs from platelet transfus…

title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery versus chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer.
abstract: Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the primary treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). However, CRT is associated with high toxicity, and access to radiotherapy infrastructure remains limited or unavailable in some settings globally. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) followed by radical surgery has therefore been proposed as an alternative to CRT, but the evidence regarding its efficacy and toxicity compared to CRT remains unclear. To compare NACT followed by radical surgery versus CRT for…

title: Surgical interventions for adults with low back pain with or without spine-related leg pain or degenerative lumbar spinal abnormalities: an overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (overview). The objectives are as follows: To summarise systematic reviews that assess the effects of surgical interventions for adults with low back pain with or without spine-related leg pain or degenerative lumbar spinal abnormalities.

title: Interventions for managing immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps.
abstract: Immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps are difficult candidates for conventional root canal fillings. Interventions for management of such teeth include regenerative endodontic procedures (REPs), apexification, and root strengthening interventions. Basic principles involve removal of necrotic pulp, canal debridement and infection control. Currently, there is no evidence-based guidance to manage such teeth. To assess the effects of different interventions to manage immature permanent teeth…

title: World Health Organization non-laboratory-based 10-year cardiovascular disease risk prediction model in adults without established disease.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (prognosis). The objectives are as follows: The objective of this review is to evaluate the prognostic performance of the World Health Organization (WHO) non-laboratory-based CVD risk prediction models in adults aged 40 years to 74 years without established CVD. title: Curcuma longa (turmeric) or its active ingredients for osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a major cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments have limited efficacy. Curcuma longa (turmeric) contains curcuminoids with anti-inflammatory properties that may modulate osteoarthritis pathophysiology. However, the clinical benefits and safety of Curcuma longa in osteoarthritis remain uncertain. To assess the benefits and harms of Curcuma longa extracts or сurcuminoids for osteoarthritis. title: Low-dose oral misoprostol for induction of labour.
abstract: Oral misoprostol is a common labour induction method. This review is restricted to lower doses (initially ≤ 50 µg), as higher doses pose unacceptably high risks of uterine hyperstimulation. To assess the benefits and harms of low-dose oral misoprostol for labour induction in women with a viable fetus in the third trimester of pregnancy, compared with other methods of labour induction.
